Basheer & Ors, 2014 SCC Online SC 732 " that any documentary evidence by way of Electronic record under the Evidence Act, in view of Section 59 and 65A, can be proved only in accordance with the procedure prescribed under Section 65B.

entities.text: Anvar P.V. Vs. P.K. Basheer & Ors, 2014 SCC Online SC 732
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Section 65B deals with the admissibility of the electronic record.
The purpose of these provisions is to sanctify secondary evidence in electronic form, generated by a computer.
It may be noted that the Section starts with a non-obstante clause.

Thus, notwithstanding anything contained in the Evidence Act, any information contained in an electronic record which is printed on a paper, stored, recorded or copied in optical or magnetic media produced by a computer shall be deemed to be a document only if the condition mentioned under sub-Section (2) are satisfied, without further proof or the production of the original.

Before proceedings further, this court deems fit to discuss the emote of the term 'cause of action.'

In the case titled as "Somi Atamananda Vs. Siri Ram Kumar Tapobana,
2005 10 SCC 51, the expression 'cause of action' has been defined to me every fact, which if traversed it would be necessary for plaintiff to prove in order to support his right to the judgment of the court,
though, it does not comprise every piece of evidence which is necessary to be proved.

sentences.text: In the present case, the plaintiffs have not mentioned a single averment as to what right of the plaintiffs have been infringed by the defendant and as to what cause of action the plaintiffs have against the defendants.

Section 477 of The Delhi Municipal Corporation Act, 1957 provides for protection of action of a Corporation, etc. and lays down that :-
"No suit or prosecution shall be entertained in any court against a Corporation or against any municipal authority or against any municipal officer or other municipal employee or against any person acting under the order or direction of any municipal authority or any municipal officer or other municipal employee, for anything, which in good faith done or intended to be done, under this Act or any rule, regulation or bye-law made thereunder."
Section 478 of The Delhi Municipal Corporation Act, 1957 provides for notice to be given of the suits and lays down that :-
"(1) No suit shall be instituted against a Corporation or against any municipal authority or against any municipal officer or other municipal employee or against any person acting under the order or direction of any municipal authority or any municipal officer or other municipal employee, in respect of any act done, or purporting to have been done in pursuance of this Act or any rule, regulation or bye-law made thereunder until the expiration of two months after notice in writing has been left at the municipal office and in case of such officer or employee or person,

(2) No suit, such as is described in sub-section(1), shall unless it is a suit for the recovery of immovable property or for a declaration of title thereto, be instituted after Sonia Verma vs Ajay Garg on 7 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104065303/

(3) Nothing in sub-section (1) shall be deemed to apply to a suit in which the only relief claimed is an injunction of which the object would be defeated by the giving of notice or the postponement of the institution of the suit."

Clause 3 of the said section specifically states that there is no need to give notice of the suit in which the only relief claimed is an injunction of which the object would be defeated by giving the notice or the postponement of the institution of the suit.

In the present case, the relief sought by the plaintiff is not of such a nature that the object of institution of the suit would be defeated if the statutory notice as mentioned in Section 478 of DMC Act, 1957 was given to the defendant no. 7/MCD.
Therefore, the present suit is also barred u/s 478 of DMC Act, 1957.
Therefore, the plaintiffs have failed to prove their case.
Accordingly, the issue no. 1 and 2 are decided against the plaintiffs and in favour of the defendants.
